Only All-Father can read or delete them. A deletion is itself recorded, with a snapshot of the deleted row. Changes are recorded with before and after values.
- **Staff login:** three fields: organization (ID or name), staff identifier (ID, username or email), password. The organization determines the server. The mapping lives in the Worker (`organizations.server_url`, NULL = this server) and is maintained by All-Father.

- Worker: 260 tests pass, 1 todo. Admin Slint: 9 unit tests pass, clippy clean, app starts under a virtual display.

## Decisions recorded 2026-11-15

Owner-approved wording:

- Policy evaluation labels: Evaluation result / نمایش نتیجه ارزیابی; Policy version / نسخه سیاست; Rule not found / قانون یافت نشد; No value defined / مقداری تعریف نشده است. The result is shown as the Worker returns it, with the evaluated policy version beside it. A missing rule or null value is never shown as false.
- Concurrency error codes (stable identifiers, not translated): LIFECYCLE_EPOCH_REQUIRED (missing lifecycle epoch), AUTHORITY_EPOCH_REQUIRED (missing authority epoch), EPOCH_MISMATCH (record changed; refresh before continuing), VERSION_CONFLICT (object version conflict). The UI maps these codes to text; it does not infer causes from error text. The Worker must return these codes; that change is not yet implemented.

Owner-approved 2026-11-15:

- Farsi: "Staff ID, username or email" = شناسه کارمند، نام کاربری یا ایمیل (applied to fa.json on this branch). "Apply legal hold" = اعمال دستور منع تغییر (to be applied on the legal-holds branch, where that key exists).

Ordinary staff and organization-admin operations stay under their normal authorization rules. All-Father must not bypass tenant isolation on generic queries or commands. Unknown and unauthorized actions stay denied. All privileged actions are auditable.

Implementation requirement (already decided earlier): ONYX ID is the primary login identifier; username and email remain aliases; the Worker login must accept all three and enforce a password change when must_change_password is set.

```rust
    Failed,
```

But `UsersError` is used in many match statements — adding a variant requires updating all matches. ```rust

Implementation:

```rust
pub(crate) fn error_code(body: &str) -> Option<String> {
    let value: Value = serde_json::from_str(body).ok()?;
    // Worker returns either {error:{code}} or {error:"CODE"}.
    match value.get("error") {
        Some(Value::String(code)) => Some(code.clone()),
        Some(Value::Object(obj)) => obj.get("code").and_then(Value::as_str).map(str::to_string),
        _ => None,
    }
}

pub(crate) fn concurrency_code(code: &str) -> Option<ConcurrencyCode> { ... }
```

Then `check_response`:

```rust
pub(crate) async fn check(response: reqwest::Response) -> Result<reqwest::Response, UsersError> {
    let status = response.status();
    if status.is_success() { return Ok(response); }
    if status == StatusCode::FORBIDDEN { return Err(UsersError::Forbidden); }
    let body = response.text().await.unwrap_or_default();
    if let Some(code) = error_code(&body).as_deref().and_then(concurrency_code) {
        return Err(UsersError::Conflict(code));
    }
    Err(UsersError::Failed)
}
```

# a real schema to check queries against -- placed after migrations
      # run above, not before.
      # Pinned to the workspace's own sqlx version: `sqlx prepare` writes
      # a per-column `origin` field that older releases don't emit, so an
      # unpinned install silently invalidates every committed `.sqlx` file
      # the day sqlx-cli releases a new one. Track the workspace major.minor
      # here and regenerate `.sqlx` when it moves.
      - name: Install sqlx-cli
        run: cargo install sqlx-cli --version 0.9.0 --no-default-features --features postgres,rustls --locked
      - name: Verify sqlx offline metadata is current
        run: cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace -- --all-targets
      # desktop-shell's secure_storage tests exercise the real `keyring`
      # crate against a live Secret Service, deliberately not mocked (see
      # keyring_adapter.rs's own test doc comments). A bare ubuntu-latest
      # runner has no D-Bus session bus or Secret Service daemon at all,
      # so those tests fail with "No default store has been set" — not a
      # code defect, a missing environment dependency. gnome-keyring is
      # the standard fix CI pipelines use for the `keyring` crate itself.
      - name: Start a D-Bus session and unlocked gnome-keyring (for secure_storage tests)
        run: |
          sudo apt-get install -y gnome-keyring dbus-x11
          rm -f "$HOME/.local/share/keyrings/login.keyring"
          mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/keyrings"
          echo -n "" | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock --login >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          eval "$(dbus-launch --sh-syntax)"
          echo "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "DBUS_SESSION_BUS_PID=$DBUS_SESSION_BUS_PID" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          eval "$(printf '\n' | gnome-keyring-daemon --unlock --components=secrets --daemonize)"
          echo "GNOME_KEYRING_CONTROL=$GNOME_KEYRING_CONTROL" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "SSH_AUTH_SOCK=$SSH_AUTH_SOCK" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
      - name: Test
        # The API integration/E2E tests intentionally exercise the deterministic
        # 429/500 fault-injection contract. It is enabled only for this test invocation;
        # production/default release builds above do not enable it.
        run: cargo test --workspace --release --features api-server/test-endpoints -- --test-threads=1

# Screen-by-screen structural description

Static source register for commit `d8f64889cfe4473d40d50c41b0992bd22955eb7b`. “Loading/error/empty” states below refer only to states visible in the inspected source or hook contract; no live API execution was performed.

## APP-DS — ONYX desktop shell

### DS-01 Login
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Login.tsx`. A two-region responsive authentication shell: a branded hero/operation context area and a credential card. The card contains a username input, password input, locale selector, submit button, loading label and conditional alert text. Submission invokes Rust Tauri command `login` with username/password, then navigates to `/` and passes the returned identity to the app; errors are mapped to localized messages. Browser autocomplete values are `username` and `current-password`; both inputs have `required`. Token persistence is native Rust-side, not a page field.

### DS-02 Session loading
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`. On mount, invokes `get_current_session`; during the unresolved call, displays centered `common.loadingSecureSession` text. A retry token re-runs the load. It does not expose the operational routes during loading.

### DS-03 Startup error
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`. A `role="alert"` section contains an error title, message and Retry button. The button increments the retry token, restarting the session-load effect. The actual network/IPC error categories depend on Rust and `toUserFacingError`.

### DS-04 Dashboard
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`. Uses summary/stat cards and links to major staff operations. Values are data-derived; the full rendered number and arrangement of data-dependent cards cannot be counted from the source without the live state.

### DS-05 Missions
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Missions.tsx`. Handles the `/missions` and `/missions/:missionId` route patterns with one component. Source includes a mission ID lookup input and View action, a refresh action, and a create-mission workflow with name and description. Operations go through the command/query hooks and typed command envelope.

### DS-06 Tasks
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Tasks.tsx`. Handles `/tasks` and `/tasks/:taskId` using one component. Includes task lookup, refresh, a task create workflow (title, description, optional mission ID), and a Mark Ready action. Detail/selection content depends on query state and provided route parameter.

### DS-07 Approvals
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Approvals.tsx`, with `components/ApprovalDialog/index.tsx` and `components/Dialog/AccessibleDialog.tsx`. Contains task ID lookup and an action that opens an in-webview modal dialog. Dialog displays a task title, a decision-note textarea and Cancel, Reject, Approve controls. Reject is disabled when the reason is blank; Approve is enabled while not loading even if the note is empty. The handler emits `ApproveTask` or `RejectTask` command with task ID, organization/user/device IDs and expected task version. Dialog traps Tab focus, focuses the configured textarea at open, restores prior focus at close, and closes on Escape unless busy.

### DS-08 Messaging
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Messaging.tsx`. One component serves `/messaging` and `/messaging/:conversationId`. The file defines lookup and compose/edit/action subcomponents: conversation type selection, optional parent-supergroup ID, member addition by ID and a checkbox for parent-supergroup membership, message lookup, post/edit message fields, reaction code and add/remove actions, redaction, and connection request send/accept/decline/revoke workflows. Many controls are conditional on selected conversation/message and command loading state; rendered counts are not stable from source alone.

### DS-09 Files
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Files.tsx`. One component serves `/files` and `/files/:fileAssetId`. Includes asset-ID lookup, upload destination/path field, version listing and download destination, per-version download buttons and user access actions (grant/revoke, quarantine, archive). The visible UI takes a path-like string for upload/download; the inspected form does not use a browser file picker for this upload field. Rust commands `upload_file` and `download_file` are registered by the desktop shell.

### DS-10 Notifications
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Notifications.tsx`. Notification collection view with Refresh and per-notification acknowledge controls. Feed content and number of actions depend on returned data; the presence of a notification event validator is source-confirmed, but live event behavior is not runtime-confirmed.

### DS-11 Account settings
Source: `crates/bins/desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Settings.tsx`. A single account section shows the signed-in username and a translated cloud-service note. A Log Out action calls the supplied reauthentication/logout handler. It is not a general preference page in the current component source.

## APP-AD — ONYX Admin

### AD-01 Login
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Login.tsx`. Hero and credential-card layout with username/password fields, locale selector and submit button. UI uses native Tauri `admin_login` rather than making the first credential request from the WebView. Submission records a request ID and diagnostic outcome, maps errors to an alert and routes to `/` after a valid session is stored. Password and tokens are not included in the diagnostic fields documented by the handlers.

### AD-02 Lazy route loading
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`. Suspense fallback shows centered `common.loadingAdmin` text while one of the lazy page modules resolves.

### AD-03 Users
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Users.tsx`. The directory table exposes username/admin-state fields and each user's class, parent and active status. A creation workflow collects username, email, password and class. Existing row actions set class, assign parent, and deactivate/reactivate. The user collection length determines row/control counts. API calls in the source include `GET /api/admin/users`, `POST /api/admin/users`, and user-specific class/parent/status paths.

### AD-04 Policy and settings
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Settings.tsx`. A single settings component hosts separate panels for mobile-access allowed classes, ID lookup, policy creation, policy version/rule drafting and actions, and legal holds. Controls are conditional on selected policy/hold ID and request state. The source includes class checkboxes, policy-name/key/value inputs, rule-type select, rule add/submit, publish/retire/evaluate, and legal-hold target UUID/type/reason and release lookup. Exact live row counts depend on fetched records and dynamic rules.

### AD-05 Staff profiles
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Profiles.tsx`. Lists profile records, allows opening an edit overlay, and exposes batch import/export. The profile shape in TypeScript includes profile/owner IDs, full name, photo blob key, job title, contact email/phone, department, class label, parent display name and a string-array team memberships field. Editable scalar fields are rendered through a reusable Field component; team memberships use a separate control. Import accepts only CSV/JSON extensions and MIME values in inspected source. Export buttons produce CSV or JSON files.

### AD-06 Organizations
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Organizations.tsx`. Lists organization cards, creates an organization from a required name (maximum 160 characters), allows renaming and activation/deactivation for eligible organizations, and displays selected organization's Admin accounts. The admin creation workflow collects username, contact email and initial password (minimum length 8); these fields/actions are disabled when busy or the selected organization is inactive. The organization route and navigation item are client-gated by role `ALL_FATHER`; the source explicitly says backend authorization is the actual boundary.

### AD-07 Admin access required
Source: `crates/bins/admin-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`. An authenticated user whose stored `is_admin` flag is false receives an access-required message naming the username and a Log Out control rather than the admin workspace.

## Overlays and nested state

- **DS-DLG-01 Approval dialog:** `desktop-shell/ui/src/components/ApprovalDialog/index.tsx`; rendered only when its `open` property is true.
- **AD-DLG-01 Profile edit overlay:** `admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Profiles.tsx`; opened by the New/Edit actions and closed/saved via callback. It is a React-rendered overlay, not a separately registered native window.
- Organization selection and admin panels, policy version/rule subpanels, message details, connection actions, and file version/ACL controls are conditional regions inside their owning page rather than declared top-level windows.

The report separates route templates from overlays. A complete DOM snapshot count for each state has not been obtained.

### 1.1.1 Screen-by-screen parity matrix (baseline contract)

This matrix is the migration's **required parity baseline**, not a claim that every behavior is runtime verified. Current-source features below are confirmed from the desktop forensic inventory and its `screen-inventory.csv` / `interactive-elements.csv`; runtime/backend outcomes and complete dynamic control-instance counts remain test obligations. Every lane must update its row with the final Slint file, automated test ID, per-OS manual result, and disposition for any approved deviation before its gate can pass.
In the source-path column, paths beginning with `admin-shell/` or `desktop-shell/` are relative to `crates/bins/`; repository-root paths are written with their full `crates/...` or `docs/...` prefix. The companion CSV is a tracking artifact; `NOT RUN` means no result has been claimed.

| Plan ID | Current source / route or state | Required Slint parity: controls and interactions | States and validation to preserve | Authorization/backend boundary | Minimum acceptance evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AD-01 | `admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Login.tsx`; `/login` | Username, password, locale switch, submit; visible busy feedback | Empty/invalid input, submitting, rejected/network error, success; never pre-fill password | Native Admin login bridge → canonical Worker `/api/auth/login`; do not invent endpoints | Unit tests for validation/error mapping; mock success/failure UI tests; Windows/Linux keyboard and Persian rendering checks |
| AD-02 | `admin-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`; lazy `Suspense` fallback | Centered loading status while a lazy page resolves | Loading then resolved content; no false authenticated state | No authorization granted by loading state | Deterministic test with delayed page/module fixture; no stuck loading on resolve |
| AD-03 | `admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Users.tsx`; `/` and `/users` | User table; create user username/email/password/class; per-user class, parent, activate/deactivate actions; preserve repeated row actions | Loading/error/empty/list; create/update busy; invalid/duplicate/server failure; row action error | Authenticated organization admin in UI; Worker remains enforcement boundary; tenant-scope errors remain visible as translated messages | Fixture-backed test of each action/error; verify server-returned canonical row after success/failure; table paging/sort/search only where current behavior exists or approved as an explicit parity enhancement |
| AD-04 | `admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Settings.tsx`; `/settings`, `/settings/:policyId` | Mobile-access class checkboxes, policy ID lookup, policy create, rule type/key/value, add rule, submit/save, publish/retire and policy actions, legal-hold actions | Loading/error/draft/lookup/validation/concurrency conflict/reload/retry-with-idempotency/success; never lose canonical server state on conflict | Worker policy/mobile-access routes plus existing command/query bridge; U-04 policy state diagram is a hard dependency for state-changing actions | Contract fixtures for documented request/response/errors; state-transition tests against approved diagram; conflict and ambiguous-create retry tests |
| AD-05 | `admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Profiles.tsx`; `/profiles` | Profile table; create/edit overlay; owner ID, full name, job title, department, email, phone, class, parent, photo key, memberships; CSV/JSON import/export | Loading/error/empty/edit/validation/import summary/export busy/row-level failures | Admin profile Worker routes; no Excel/XLSX capability may be claimed because current transfer accepts CSV/JSON | Field-by-field fixture tests, malformed import cases, CSV and JSON round-trip tests, per-row error summary; Q-05 resolved before screen starts |
| AD-06 | `admin-shell/ui/src/pages/Organizations.tsx`; `/organizations` | Organization list/create/rename/activate/deactivate; select organization; manage organization admins; admin create username/email/password and status actions | Loading/error/empty/busy/inactive-organization constraints; name max length 160; admin password minimum length 8 | Canonical `ALL_FATHER` principal and Worker routes are authoritative; client route/navigation guard is UX only | Positive/negative role fixture tests; verify organizations absent for non-All-Father; boundary validation tests; no live account assumed |
| AD-07 | `admin-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`; authenticated user where `is_admin` is false | Access-denied explanation and logout action | Denied state, logout busy/error, return to logged-out flow | Client check is not a security boundary; Worker enforces authority | Test non-admin login response shows denial; protected calls are still denied by mocked Worker policy; logout clears only approved session storage |
| DS-01 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Login.tsx`; conditional when no persisted session | Username/password, locale selector, sign-in | Required fields, submitting, auth/network failure, successful authenticated transition; password never stored by UI | Slint callbacks call existing Rust session/auth implementation; Rust calls canonical Worker; tokens remain native | Mock authentication tests; prove tokens are not passed into Slint properties; Windows/Linux login, keyboard, language/IME checks |
| DS-02 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`; session undefined during startup/retry | Centered loading status | Loading → login or authenticated shell; no stale session exposure | Rust `get_current_session`; returned `SessionInfo` excludes access/refresh tokens | State test for `None`/session/success and delayed completion; confirm no token appears in Slint model/logs |
| DS-03 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/App.tsx`; `startupError` | Alert/title/message and Retry | Error then retry; repeated failure does not crash or expose authenticated screen | Startup IPC/session load path; keep current failure behavior unless contract change approved | Tests for initial load rejection, retry success and repeated failure |
| DS-04 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`; `/` | Summary/stat cards and three source-confirmed quick links | Data-dependent values, loading/error/empty where current hooks expose them | Local Rust query/sync status path; no invented remote source | Fixture-backed view-model test, route tests, missing/empty data states |
| DS-05 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Missions.tsx`; `/missions`, `/missions/:missionId` | Shared shell navigation; refresh; mission-ID lookup; mission name/description; create | Loading/error/empty/list/detail/lookup validation/create busy and error; trim/require nonblank name | `GetMission` query and `CreateMission` command through local Rust registry | Registry adapter schema tests; valid/invalid ID cases; create/refresh/lookup tests |
| DS-06 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Tasks.tsx`; `/tasks`, `/tasks/:taskId` | Task ID lookup; title/description/mission ID; create; Mark Ready | Loading/error/lookup/create busy; blank title disabled; invalid ID handling; status transition result | `GetTask`, `CreateTask`, `MarkReady` through local registry; preserve ID wire format until Q-16 resolution is applied to display only | Command/query fixtures, ID parse/round trip tests, action authorization/error tests |
| DS-07 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Approvals.tsx` and `ApprovalDialog` | Task ID lookup; review action; decision-note textarea; Cancel, Reject, Approve | Selected-submission/review states; dialog open/closed; busy; reject requires nonblank reason; server failure | Local query/command registry plus hierarchy/approval authority cache; never infer approval authority from UI alone | Positive/negative authority tests; dialog keyboard/focus tests; submit/cancel/error tests; two-OS manual check |
| DS-08 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Messaging.tsx`; `/messaging`, `/:conversationId` | Conversation type/list/detail; parent Supergroup ID for SubTeam; add member; member mode; compose/edit/reaction/redact; connection actions | Loading/error/empty/selection; create/post/edit/reaction/redact states; SubTeam parent ID parse; reject blank message; connection pending/accepted/declined/revoked; reconnect/resync | Local command/query/event API; current source has event subscription with no matching unsubscribe command. Do not invent multi-client guarantees; U-08 and U-11 must be resolved before messaging implementation | Two-client event/ordering/reconnect/resync tests; event lifecycle/leak tests; malformed ID and blank-message validation; manual two-OS scenario |
| DS-09 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Files.tsx`; `/files`, `/:fileAssetId` | Asset ID lookup; upload path/action; file version list; download destination/action; ACL user ID; grant/revoke/quarantine/archive | Loading/error/empty/selected/upload/download busy/failure; enforce 100 MiB client limit only if still confirmed by current contract; path and ID validation | Native `upload_file`/`download_file` plus registered file-domain commands; OS path handling in D12 | Temp-directory upload/download round trip on Windows/Linux; permissions and error tests; ACL command tests; no guessed native file dialog unless Q/design approves it |
| DS-10 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Notifications.tsx`; `/notifications` | Refresh; notification feed; per-item acknowledge | Loading/error/empty/acknowledging/ack success/failure; event refresh | Local notification query/command and event subscription; OS-native notifications are separate Q-09/U-09 scope | Fixture UI tests, ack idempotence/error tests; OS notification tests only for explicitly approved event/scope |
| DS-11 | `desktop-shell/ui/src/pages/Settings.tsx`; `/settings` | Account identity/status and sign-out/re-authentication callback | Current identity, logout busy/error, return to DS-01 | `get_current_session` / `logout` native Rust behavior; tokens never enter Slint UI state | Logout clears session and person-dependent cache; next launch returns to login; no raw token exposure |

**Shared shell contract (not an extra route screen):** the authenticated Desktop shell retains eight primary navigation entries (Overview, Missions, Tasks, Approvals, Messaging, Files, Notifications, Settings), active-route indication, and the existing narrow-layout drawer behavior where it is part of current functionality. The native target is a desktop UI, but do not silently delete responsive shell behavior just because it originated in CSS; the owner must either preserve it or record an approved parity deviation. Admin navigation retains Users, Policy Settings, and Staff Profiles for organization admins; Organizations is shown only for `ALL_FATHER`. All authorization remains server-side.

**Control count rule:** the audit's literal JSX counts (Desktop: 39 buttons, 22 inputs, 3 textareas, 1 select; Admin: 29 buttons, 22 inputs, 0 textareas, 4 selects; table/form counts are also documented in the audit) are source-structure counts, not a runtime exhaustive total. `interactive-elements.csv` is a confirmed minimum inventory with dynamic-template caveats. Each Slint screen lane must add stable test IDs and document repeated controls using representative fixtures; it must not claim exact runtime instance parity from static counts alone.

### 1.2 Known unknowns (must be resolved before Contract Freeze)
These are facts the audit did not establish. BOUND says a contract cannot be frozen while a neighbour still needs to ask about externally visible behaviour.

| ID | Unknown | Blocks | Investigation owner |

| U-03 | Bundled font covering Latin and Persian glyphs with correct shaping | C-04 theme tokens | D13 + D3 font selection |
| U-04 | Policy state diagram (states and allowed transitions) | C-02 for AD-04 | User decision |
| U-05 | Mission/task ID format in the new UI (Farsi digits or Latin) | C-02 for DS-05, DS-06, C-06 | Q-16 (Farsi IDs in Latin digits?) |
| U-06 | Windows code signing capability and certificate availability | Packaging contract, Wave 5 | User decision |
| U-07 | Installer tool choice (NSIS, MSI, other; Linux AppImage vs .deb) | Packaging contract, Wave 5 | User decision |
| U-08 | Messaging multi-client behaviour (not verified by audit; state sync, connection loss recovery) | C-02 for DS-08, B-11f | Investigation lane, read desktop registry |
| U-09 | Native OS notification scope and permission model per OS | C-02 for DS-10, B-11d | User decision |
| U-10 | Reduce-motion setting access per OS in Slint runtime | C-05 animation hooks, B-12 | D13 spike |
| U-11 | Desktop event subscription lifecycle: `subscribe_events` returns an ID but the current Tauri command set has no matching unsubscribe; define safe cancellation/teardown in native Slint host | C-02 Desktop adapter, B-11f, integration tests | D13 + Desktop integration owner |
| U-12 | Complete dark theme token set and contrast pairs (the Phase 0 Slint scaffold only defines a minimal token subset) | C-04, C-05, Gate 0b | D3 + D13 contrast tests |

## 4. Executable Team Briefs

Each brief is self-contained. A lane can start from its brief and the frozen contracts, with mocks, and without asking neighbours for internal details.

Common rules for every brief:
- Owned files only. Edits outside them require the owner's approval.
- Use mocks from D13 fixtures until the real neighbour merges.
- Every brief ends with a deliverable checklist and a test list.
- Tauri/React apps and the current Tauri release remain in place through Gate 5. No Tauri/React removal occurs before Gate 6 approval and a separate approved removal PR.

### Brief B-01: Worker Client (D1)
- **Mission:** Implement Worker calls for Admin, returning typed results. No UI code.
- **Consumes:** C-01 (endpoints and bodies, at pinned repository baseline `b056c6ef204080446e84b31f3d35a226e6a40867`; Worker source baseline `38c8975fd6616376d51e016b3e718b7736888514`), C-09 (fixtures).
- **Provides:** C-03 (error taxonomy), C-02 Rust-side functions for Admin screens.
- **Files:** `src/client/mod.rs`, `src/client/login.rs` (move from PR #304 logic), `src/client/users.rs`, `src/client/profiles.rs`, `src/client/policy.rs`, `src/client/orgs.rs`.
- **Rules:** 30 s timeout; canonical base URL constant; errors classified, never raw bodies; no passwords in logs or errors; every endpoint in use is documented in C-01.
- **Mock:** fixture server in D13 (`tests/fixtures/`).
- **Tests:** one test per endpoint per success and per error class; timeout test; malformed-response test; contract test (request shape and response shape match C-01).
- **Forbidden assumptions:** do not invent endpoints. Every call must map to a row in `api-contract.md`.
- **Verification:** V-05 (endpoint coverage), V-06 (fixture schema), V-07 (error mapping).

### Brief B-02: Session & Secrets (D2)
- **Mission:** Session state machine and keyring storage (remembered username; tokens for Admin pending Q-01).
- **Consumes:** C-03, C-07, C-08, C-09.
- **Provides:** C-07 (session states), C-08 (storage operations).
- **Files:** `src/session/state.rs`, `src/session/store.rs`, `src/session/keyring_adapter.rs`.
- **Auth contracts (TBD):** Read `crates/bins/admin-shell/src/session.rs` (or equivalent) and Worker auth routes. Document token expiry, refresh, revocation, logout, startup restore, and password handling rules. These go into the final C-07 detail.
- **Rules:** All-Father never writes authentication/session state; passwords are never stored. Implement token refresh only according to the verified Worker/session contract; do not assume proactive refresh, silent refresh, or retry behavior before the source read and contract freeze. Keyring-failure behavior must follow the approved C-07/C-08 rule rather than silently treating every storage failure as logged out.
- **Tests:** state transitions; remembered-username rules; All-Father skip; keyring error path (returns notice, not panic); token expiry and refresh cycles; logout clears all state.
- **Platform check:** keyring tests run on Linux (with a secret service, as the existing CI does) and Windows.
- **Verification:** V-08 (session transitions), V-09 (keyring contract), V-11 (passwords never stored).

### Brief B-03: Design System (D3)
- **Mission:** Components and theme tokens, light and dark; font bundling; accessibility support.
- **Consumes:** C-04 (tokens, after U-03 spike), U-01, U-02, U-10 findings from spikes.
- **Provides:** C-05 (component API), C-04 (final token set), accessible components per OS.
- **Files:** `ui/theme.slint`, `ui/components/*.slint` (button, text-field, password-field, checkbox, select, table, multiline-input, dialog, toast, stat-card, nav-item, status-badge, combobox).
- **Rules:** every colour from `Theme`; focus ring in both themes; components expose properties and callbacks only, no business logic; accessibility: labels, screen-reader output, keyboard navigation per OS (Windows UI Automation, Linux AT-SPI); bidirectional text support (RTL/LTR per field); reduce-motion support per U-10.
- **Tests:** Slint compile of every component; contrast test for every token pair (WCAG AA); API snapshot test (names of properties and callbacks); accessibility manual test per OS; bidirectional text rendering test; reduce-motion test.
- **Font:** bundled font (U-03 spike result) covering Latin a-z and Persian script with correct shaping, plus digits if needed per C-06 decision.
- **Freedom:** internal layout and animation details are local decisions.
- **Verification:** V-03 (component API snapshot), V-04 (theme contrast), per-OS accessibility manual checks.

### Brief B-04: Localization (D4)
- **Mission:** Keys and values for `en` and `fa`; digit conventions; language and theme persistence (Q-14).
- **Consumes:** none (keys come from screen briefs).
- **Provides:** C-06 (localization contract).
- **Files:** `src/i18n.rs`.
- **Rules:** every key has both values; no key is removed without a change note (3.3); use the single approved Latin-or-Farsi display convention for mission/task IDs from Q-16 (not a per-session/per-user setting unless separately approved); field-by-field RTL/LTR behavior per C-06.
- **Tests:** exhaustiveness test (every `Key` used in `ui/` appears in `i18n.rs`); non-empty test (exists); digit-format tests (Latin and Farsi); RTL/LTR test (cursor movement, selection, copy/paste).
- **Persistence (Q-14):** if yes, record an explicit choice of separate non-secret preference storage, restore timing, corrupt/unavailable-storage behavior, and whether this preference persistence applies to All-Father. Do not store theme/language inside authentication tokens or the auth-session record by default. If no, start from defaults (English, light) each launch. Q-14 remains open until the owner records this decision.
- **Verification:** V-01 (localization completeness), V-02 (exhaustive translations), V-06 (localization keys in C-06).

### Brief B-05: Login (D5) — first screen, AD-01
- **Mission:** Phase 1 login screen per the planning document.
- **Consumes:** C-02 (login view model), C-03, C-04, C-05, C-06, C-07, C-08.
- **Provides:** a working login flow that uses mocks first, then the real client.
- **Files:** `ui/screens/login.slint`, `src/screens/login.rs`.
- **Phase 1 spec (from planning doc):**
  - Right panel: login form (username, password, remember-username checkbox, show/hide password toggle, submit button).
  - Left panel: placeholder for animation (visual space, not interactive).
  - Remember checkbox: saves username to keyring; does NOT save password. Password always asked at next login.
  - All-Father login: remember checkbox disabled; no state stored; password required every time.
  - Dark mode and light mode buttons (theme toggle).
  - Farsi and English buttons (language toggle).
  - Multi-language: all UI text in the form per C-06. Arabic/Farsi text right-to-left, English left-to-right per field.
  - Error messages: per C-03 error codes (e.g., `LOGIN_AUTH_REJECTED`). Translated per C-06.
  - Loading state: submit button disabled; spinner shown.
  - Accessibility: labels tied to fields; screen-reader output per OS; keyboard navigation (Tab, Enter, Escape).
- **Tests:** empty fields disable submit; loading state transitions correctly; each error code shows the right text (per C-03, C-06); remember-username saved and restored; remember-username cleared if user clears checkbox; password never stored or pre-filled; show/hide password toggle works; theme and language switches work; All-Father: remember disabled; tab order correct; screen reader reads all labels.
- **Gate:** Gate 2 first integrated path; foundation tests pass at Gate 1, then user signs off the per-screen login checklist.

### Brief B-06: Shell and Access (D6) — AD-02, AD-07 (Admin), Desktop session loading/startup error (DS-02/DS-03)
- **Mission:** Main frame/navigation, Admin loading and access-denied states, and Desktop session-loading/startup-error states with retry.
- **Consumes:** C-07, C-05, C-06.
- **Provides:** frame slot for screen teams D7 to D11.
- **Files:** `ui/screens/shell.slint`, `src/screens/shell.rs`.
- **Rules:** navigation items come from one frozen list per app; Admin Organizations is shown only for `ALL_FATHER`; the Worker remains the authority and the UI respects 403. Desktop `get_current_session` errors currently produce the DS-03 startup error with retry; do not silently convert storage errors into a successful logged-out state. Admin keyring behavior follows Q-01 and C-08. Logout clears the app's session state according to its tested Rust/client contract.
- **Tests:** navigation visibility per role; access-denied path (non-admin); logout clears state; startup retry on connection error; Farsi and English text directions correct; theme changes apply to frame; accessibility: navigation items navigable by keyboard, screen-reader announces current screen.
- **Startup states (sequence):**
  1. Resolve startup session using each app's frozen C-07/C-08 behavior (Desktop current source reads `StoredSession` via `SecureStorage`; Admin behavior follows Q-01).
  2. Admin: while lazy page content loads, show AD-02; unauthenticated state routes to AD-01.
  3. Desktop: no stored session routes to DS-01; while `get_current_session` is unresolved show DS-02; a rejected startup read shows DS-03 with retry; a valid session mounts the authenticated shared shell.
  4. Login failure shows the translated login error state; retry is used only where the current flow provides retry.
  5. Admin authenticated but non-admin user sees AD-07. Desktop does not claim a standalone access-denied screen unless a source-confirmed route/state is added to the matrix.

```rust
//! Display-only digit normalization for identifiers (Q-16 / U-05).
//!
//! Decision (2026-10-27): IDs are shown with Latin digits in every locale.
//! This is display-only. Stored values, serialization, identifiers, and API
//! data are never changed. Call this only at the rendering boundary.

/// Returns `s` with Persian (U+06F0–U+06F9) and Arabic-Indic (U+0660–U+0669)
/// digits replaced by ASCII digits. All other characters are unchanged.
pub fn latin_digits(s: &str) -> String {
    s.chars()
        .map(|c| match c {
            '\u{06F0}'..='\u{06F9}' => char::from(b'0' + (c as u32 - 0x06F0) as u8),
            '\u{0660}'..='\u{0669}' => char::from(b'0' + (c as u32 - 0x0660) as u8),
            other => other,
        })
        .collect()
}
```

```ts
/**
 * Display-only digit formatting for identifiers (decision Q-16 / U-05).
 *
 * Persian (U+06F0–U+06F9) and Arabic-Indic (U+0660–U+0669) digits are shown as
 * Latin 0–9. This never changes the stored value: canonical data, serialization,
 * identifiers, and API payloads keep the original characters. Use only when
 * rendering; never pass the result back to the API or store it.
 */
const PERSIAN_DIGITS = "۰۱۲۳۴۵۶۷۸۹";
const ARABIC_INDIC_DIGITS = "٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩";

export function toLatinDigits(value: string): string {
  let out = "";
  for (const ch of value) {
    const p = PERSIAN_DIGITS.indexOf(ch);
    const a = ARABIC_INDIC_DIGITS.indexOf(ch);
    if (p !== -1) out += String(p);
    else if (a !== -1) out += String(a);
    else out += ch;
  }
  return out;
}

// Unicode isolates keep an identifier LTR inside RTL text, so separators such as
// "-" do not move to the wrong side. Applied by IdText only, not by toLatinDigits.
const LRI = "⁦";
const PDI = "⁩";

export function isolateLtr(text: string): string {
  return `${LRI}${text}${PDI}`;
}
```
